{{distinguish|Spherical photo}}
In [[differential geometry]], the '''spherical image''' of a [[Curve#Length of a curve|unit-speed curve]] is given by taking the curve's [[tangent vector]]s as points, all of which must lie on the [[unit sphere]]. The movement of the spherical image describes the changes in the original curve's direction<ref>O'Neill, B. ''Elementary Differential Geometry'', 1961, pg 71.</ref>   If <math>\alpha</math> is a unit-speed curve, that is <math> \|\alpha^\prime \| = 1</math>, and <math>T</math> is the [[Frenet frame|unit tangent vector field]] along <math>\alpha</math>, then the curve <math>\sigma =  T </math> is the spherical image of <math>\alpha</math>. All points of <math>\sigma</math> must lie on the unit sphere because <math>\|\sigma\| = \| T\| = 1</math>.
